KHÚC DẠO ĐẦU — NGÀY THIÊN ĐÀNG BIẾT ĐẾN CHIẾN TRANH

✦

Mảnh tháp đầu tiên rơi giữa họ.

Nó xuyên qua cánh một thiên thần đang bò khỏi khe nứt, ghim người ấy xuống nền pha lê. Tiếng kêu bật ra rồi mất hút giữa tiếng kim loại. Lucifer quay đầu. Trên cao, phần còn lại của ngọn tháp đã nghiêng khỏi móng, chậm chạp phủ bóng lên cả hai đạo quân.

Michael cũng nhìn thấy. “Giữ bên trái.”

Lucifer chưa kịp nghĩ xem mình có còn nhận lệnh từ chàng hay không. Đôi cánh đã mở.

Gió quật tro khỏi quảng trường. Ở phía đối diện, Michael cắm kiếm xuống nền đá. Hai đầu gối chàng chùng đi khi sức nặng của ngọn tháp dồn vào lưỡi kiếm. Những đường sáng chạy dọc bộ giáp bạc, lóe lên ở chỗ vai giáp đã vỡ rồi tắt phụt.

Khối tháp khựng lại trên đầu họ, chỉ trong một nhịp. Lucifer đưa tay. Y không cố giữ lấy sức nặng Michael đang gánh; y bẻ hướng rơi của nó. Hàng nghìn phiến quang chất cọ vào nhau, rít lên. Một nửa trượt về phía tây, một nửa đổ sang đông, lướt sát trên những hàng khiên trước khi văng khỏi rìa quảng trường.

Mảnh cuối cùng sượt qua cánh Lucifer. Mùi lông cháy lẫn vào tro. Khi bầu trời mở ra trở lại, hai đạo quân vẫn còn đó.

Vài người ngẩng lên, dường như đã quên mình phải nâng kiếm về phía nào. Một thiên thần bên hàng ngũ Michael buông khiên, lao đến kéo chiến binh phản nghịch bị ghim dưới mảnh tháp. Người bị thương giật tay lại theo bản năng. Cả hai nhìn nhau một thoáng, rồi cùng nắm vào phiến đá.

Michael không ngăn họ. Lucifer thấy bàn tay chàng vẫn đặt trên chuôi kiếm.

Ở gần khe nứt, Healiangel đã quỳ bên thiên thần vừa rơi. Ánh sáng chảy khỏi phần cánh bị xuyên, phủ lên hai cổ tay anh. Anh cúi rất thấp, gần như ôm lấy vết thương để giữ nó khỏi chấn động khi nền quảng trường bên dưới tiếp tục nứt ra.

Một chiến binh từ phía Thiên Đàng chạy tới. Mazikeen bước ngang qua, kiếm đen dựng lên trước ngực người ấy.

“Lùi lại.”

“Hắn là người của ta.”

Mazikeen liếc xuống Healiangel. “Vậy thì để hắn sống trước đã.”

Nàng hất cằm về phía đôi tay đang chữa lành.

Người kia không lùi, nhưng cũng không bước tiếp.

Healiangel không nhìn ai. “Nếu còn muốn nhận lại hắn, đừng làm nền đá rung nữa.”

Mazikeen xoay thanh kiếm xuống. Thiên thần đối diện chậm rãi hạ vũ khí theo.

Một tiếng rền chạy dưới chân Lucifer. Khe nứt giữa quảng trường mở thêm. Ánh sáng từ sâu bên dưới hắt lên gương mặt Michael, làm đường cắt từ thái dương xuống gò má chàng hiện rõ. Vết thương còn mới. Lucifer nhận ra đường kiếm của chính mình. Y nhớ lực va truyền ngược vào cổ tay.

Michael rút kiếm khỏi nền.

“Đủ rồi.”

Giọng chàng không lớn. Những người đứng gần vẫn nghe và siết lại đội hình.

Lucifer khép cánh. Phần lông vừa cháy cọ vào nhau, đau rát.

“Ngươi nên nói với họ.”

“Ta đang nói với ngươi.”

Michael bước đến mép khe nứt. Một phiến đá sụp khỏi chân chàng, rơi vào luồng sáng bên dưới mà không phát ra tiếng.

“Hạ kiếm.”

Lucifer nhìn xuống tay mình. Lưỡi kiếm vẫn còn ánh sáng của những kẻ đã chạm vào nó. Y không nhớ mình đã nắm chặt đến mức nào.

“Ngươi trước.”

Michael đứng yên.

Lucifer đã chờ chính sự im lặng ấy. Các ngón tay y lại siết chặt hơn.

Ở phía sau Michael, một người đang lấy chính cánh mình che cho đồng đội bị thương. Ở phía sau Lucifer, một chiến binh mất nửa cánh cố đứng thẳng vì thấy y đang nhìn.

Michael nhìn qua hai hàng quân. Bàn tay cầm kiếm của chàng hạ xuống một chút. Vài lưỡi kiếm phía sau cũng hạ theo, rồi dừng. Lucifer nới tay; chiến binh mất nửa cánh thấy vậy lại bấu chặt hơn vào chuôi vũ khí.

“Trở về.”

“Để chịu phán xét?”

“Để sống.”

Lucifer nhìn vết cắt trên mặt chàng. “Ngươi không hứa được điều đó.”

“Ta có thể đứng trước ngươi.”

“Ngươi đang đứng trước ta.”

Michael im lặng.

Từ phía khe nứt, thiên thần dưới tay Healiangel bật lên một tiếng nghẹn. Healiangel cúi sát hơn. Mazikeen nhìn Lucifer. Nàng không thúc giục. Chính điều đó khiến y khó quay đi hơn.

Michael bước qua khe nứt.

Đá vỡ dưới chân chàng nhưng không rơi. Trọng lực quanh bộ giáp ghì những mảnh vụn lại, tạo thành một lối đi chỉ đủ cho một người.

Đội hình sau lưng chàng xao động.

Michael đưa bàn tay trống ra.

“Về với ta.”

Lưỡi kiếm trong tay Lucifer hạ xuống.

Y không định làm vậy. Cổ tay chỉ bỗng nặng đi khi nhìn bàn tay kia — bàn tay từng giữ nền dưới giọng hát của y, vừa ghì cả ngọn tháp để y bẻ hướng, và lúc này đang run rất nhẹ giữa chiến trường.

Một tiếng thét vọng lên từ tầng cầu phía dưới.

Rất nhiều đôi cánh quay về phía âm thanh ấy. Đội hình Michael khép lại quanh khe nứt. Phía Lucifer, những người còn đứng được nâng vũ khí, chờ y chọn trước.

Bàn tay Michael vẫn mở.

Lucifer nhìn những ngón tay ấy. Rồi y nhìn thanh kiếm trong tay còn lại của chàng.

“Ta đã từng ở với ngươi,” y nói.

“Vẫn còn có thể.”

“Không phải theo cách ngươi muốn.”

Michael bước thêm nửa bước. Khe nứt rền dưới chân.

“Ta không muốn giết ngươi.”

Lucifer thấy cơ hàm chàng siết lại khi nói câu ấy. Trên gò má Michael, ánh sáng rịn ra khỏi vết cắt và chảy thành một đường mỏng.

“Ta biết.”

Y nâng kiếm.

Bàn tay Michael khép lại.

Trong khoảnh khắc ngắn ngủi trước khi chàng đưa nó về chuôi kiếm, Lucifer tưởng chàng sẽ gọi tước hiệu của mình. Sao Mai. Kẻ Phản Nghịch. Bất kỳ cái tên nào đủ xa để hai lưỡi kiếm có thể chạm nhau.

Michael gọi: “Samael.”

Mũi kiếm Lucifer chệch khỏi đường thẳng một đốt tay. Michael nhìn thấy, nhưng chàng không bước tới.

Sau lưng họ, những kẻ cả hai vừa cứu đã nhặt lại vũ khí.

Lucifer đưa mũi kiếm trở về. Michael rút kiếm lên.

Hai lưỡi kiếm chạm nhau. Dưới chân họ, khe nứt mở thêm.

CHƯƠNG 1 — BẢN GIAO HƯỞNG RẠN VỠ

✦

Nốt cuối trong giọng Lucifer đi hết một vòng Thiên Đàng rồi trở về dưới lòng bàn chân y.

Y biết nó sẽ trở lại vào đúng nhịp nào. Dù vậy, khi nền pha lê rung lên, y vẫn đợi thêm một thoáng để nghe phần âm vang cuối cùng tan vào những ngọn tháp.

Trước mặt y, quảng trường mở ra giữa ba tầng mây sáng. Muôn hàng thiên thần nối nhau đến nơi mắt thường không còn thấy điểm cuối. Giáp chạm giáp. Cánh xếp sau cánh. Dưới mỗi bước chân là một âm trầm được tạc sẵn trong nền đá; trên mỗi lần dang cánh là tiếng kim loại rời vỏ, nối nhau thành một lớp âm thanh phủ kín bầu trời.

Lucifer nâng tay.

Dòng sông vàng dưới chân tháp dâng khỏi bờ, uốn thành một vòng cung trên quảng trường. Giọng hát đầu tiên của y chạm vào đó. Ánh sáng tách ra thành vô số sợi, chạy dọc các hàng quân rồi quay về với những sai lệch nhỏ nhất còn mắc trong chúng.

Ba thiên thần hộ vệ bên chân tháp phía tây giữ hơi quá lâu. Một Seraphim ở tầng cao đã mở cánh trước nhịp dẫn. Ở xa hơn, một giọng trầm thấp xuống gần nửa cung khi âm thanh đi qua phần giáp vừa được rèn lại.

Lucifer xoay cổ tay.

Dòng sông vàng đổi hướng, va vào mặt tháp rồi dội trở lại. Ba hơi thở được nhả ra. Đôi cánh trên cao khựng đúng một nhịp. Giọng trầm tìm lại cao độ mà không ai trong hàng ngũ phải quay đầu nhìn người vừa hát lệch.

Ở đầu bên kia quảng trường, Michael hạ mũi kiếm xuống nền.

Chàng không dẫn giai điệu. Chàng giữ phần bên dưới nó. Mỗi khi hợp âm dâng quá cao, trọng lượng từ thanh kiếm bạc ép nền pha lê lún xuống một đường mảnh; mỗi khi ánh sáng tràn khỏi đội hình, một cử động nơi vai chàng kéo nó trở lại, gọn như mép giáp vừa khép.

Lucifer đưa bản nhạc lên.

Michael giữ cho nó có nơi đáp xuống.

Họ đã làm như thế qua nhiều kỷ nguyên đến mức không cần nhìn nhau. Nhưng ở lần chuyển cung cuối, Michael vẫn ngẩng lên. Lucifer bắt gặp ánh mắt chàng giữa hàng triệu đôi cánh. Michael nghiêng đầu rất nhẹ. Lucifer hạ ngón tay cuối cùng.

Muôn giọng hát khép lại cùng lúc.

Âm cuối đi qua những thung lũng, làm mặt các dòng sông vàng dợn lên, rồi chạm tới rìa xa nhất của cõi trời. Khi nó quay về, vẫn nguyên vẹn như lúc rời quảng trường.

Lucifer buông tay.

Một ngọn giáo rơi xuống.

Âm thanh mảnh, khô và sai chỗ. Vài hàng cánh gần cuối quảng trường quay lại trước khi kỷ luật kéo họ về tư thế cũ.

Thiên thần vừa trở về từ biên giới đang quỳ trên một gối. Mũi giáo nằm bên cạnh, chớp tắt trên nền đá. Người đi cùng cúi xuống, nắm lấy khuỷu tay người ấy.

“Đứng lên.”

Lời nói quá nhỏ để đi xa. Thiên thần canh gác chống tay xuống nền. Đầu gối trượt đi. Lồng ngực người ấy vẫn phát sáng, nhưng nhịp sáng không ăn khớp với hơi thở đang bật qua đôi môi mở.

Michael rời vị trí một bước.

Trọng lượng của chàng làm một đường tối lan dưới mặt pha lê. Chàng nhìn người lính canh, rồi nhìn sang Lucifer.

Hồi ca kế tiếp đã mở trước mặt y. Chỉ cần hạ tay, cả quảng trường sẽ đi vào nốt đầu. Nếu y giữ lại, muôn hàng thiên thần sẽ phải đứng trong một khoảng chờ chưa từng có trong nghi lễ.

Lucifer nhìn đôi tay đang run quanh cán giáo.

Thiên thần kia tự đứng lên trước khi y quyết định. Người đi cùng buông khuỷu tay người ấy và lùi về chỗ. Hàng ngũ khép lại, nhanh đến mức vị trí vừa bỏ trống biến mất giữa những bộ giáp sáng.

Michael chưa trở về hàng.

Lucifer hạ tay.

Bài ca tiếp tục.

Khi đến lượt, giọng của thiên thần canh gác nhập vào chậm nửa nhịp.

Người bên cạnh không nhìn sang. Michael đứng yên thêm một thoáng rồi mới quay về vị trí. Chỉ Lucifer giữ độ lệch ấy lại trong tai.

Những người canh rìa gọi nơi họ vừa trở về là khoảng lặng. Không có bản đồ nào ghi chúng. Ánh sáng vẫn hiện hữu ở đó nhưng không còn hơi ấm; tiếng cánh biến mất ngay sau lưng; mối dây nối mỗi thiên thần với bài ca lùi xa đến mức chính vũ khí đang nắm cũng trở nên xa lạ.

Khi ra khỏi đó, mọi thứ ập về cùng lúc. Có người ngã. Có người trở lại đội hình và không nhắc đến điều đã xảy ra.

Lucifer chưa từng bước vào một khoảng lặng. Y chỉ nghe thấy dấu nó để lại: một hơi thở không chịu về đúng nhịp, một đôi cánh khép quá chặt, một nốt hát đến muộn dù người hát chưa từng sai.

Trên quảng trường, bài ca vẫn sáng và đầy.

Nửa nhịp kia không biến mất trong đó.

✦

Điều Lucifer nhớ rõ nhất về Những Cự Thú Đầu Tiên là hơi ấm còn lại trên lòng bàn tay.

Khi Trái Đất vẫn còn phủ màu xanh thẫm của dương xỉ và rừng cổ, một cơn địa chấn đã khép hai vách núi quanh một cự thú non. Chân trước của nó bị ghim dưới phiến nham thạch. Mỗi lần nó giãy, đá trên sườn núi lại đổ xuống, còn tiếng kêu dội qua đầm lầy làm mặt nước run thành từng vòng.

Lucifer hạ xuống giữa cơn mưa.

Gió từ đôi cánh vàng ép những thân cây cổ thụ cúi rạp. Lá mục bị quét khỏi mặt đất. Những mảnh đá quanh chân y bật lên khỏi bùn và treo lơ lửng.

Con vật nhìn thấy tất cả.

Nó hất đầu, chiếc cổ dài quật gãy một thân cây. Chân bị kẹt giật mạnh. Mép đá nghiến sâu hơn vào lớp da sần, kéo theo một dòng máu đen tràn xuống bùn.

Lucifer dừng lại.

Phiến đá không đáng kể đối với y. Chỉ cần khép một ngón tay, y có thể nghiền nó thành cát. Nhưng trong đôi mắt đen và mở lớn của con vật, y chỉ là một nguồn sáng khác vừa giáng xuống giữa đất đang rung.

Y thu cánh.

Mưa rơi trở lại trên vai, làm tóc y sẫm đi. Những hòn đá đang lơ lửng rơi lộp bộp xuống bùn.

Lucifer bước tới.

Con vật gầm lên. Hơi nóng từ miệng nó thổi tung nước trên các phiến lá.

Y dừng.

Nó giật chân lần nữa. Toàn thân co lại quanh vết thương.

“Ta biết.”

Từ ngữ không thể mang nghĩa tới nó, nhưng giọng y đã hạ xuống, không còn sức ép của người dẫn hàng triệu giọng hát.

Lucifer đặt một đầu gối vào bùn và mở bàn tay.

Ở phía bên kia vách núi, tiếng gọi bầy vọng lại. Con cự thú non đáp bằng một âm thanh ngắn rồi im. Nó nhìn bàn tay trước mặt rất lâu. Mưa chảy qua những rãnh da trên trán, nhỏ xuống giữa các ngón tay Lucifer.

Chiếc cổ đồ sộ hạ dần.

Vầng trán ướt lạnh chạm vào lòng bàn tay sáng. Nhịp tim bên dưới lớp xương đập mạnh đến mức Lucifer cảm thấy nó chạy lên tận cổ tay mình.

Y đợi.

Khi nhịp ấy chậm lại, Lucifer mới đưa tay còn lại về phía phiến đá. Nham thạch nâng lên không một tiếng động. Con vật kéo chân ra, loạng choạng lùi lại rồi quỳ sụp. Lucifer giữ phiến đá trên không cho đến khi nó tự đứng được.

Nó không bỏ chạy ngay.

Mõm dài đưa tới, chạm vào vai y. Bùn, máu và hơi thở nóng phủ lên lớp áo sáng mà nghi lễ Thiên Đàng chưa từng để dính một vết nào.

Lucifer bật ra một âm thanh rất khẽ. Về sau y không nhớ đó có phải tiếng cười hay không.

Từ bên kia núi, tiếng gọi của đàn vọng lại lần nữa. Con vật quay đầu. Nó bước được ba bước, chân trước còn kéo thành một rãnh dài trong đất, rồi dừng lại nhìn y.

Lucifer khẽ nghiêng đầu.

Con vật đi khuất sau màn mưa.

Y mang mùi đất ẩm trở về Thiên Đàng. Nó đã biến mất khỏi da trước khi y đặt chân lên bậc thềm đầu tiên, nhưng hơi ấm thì ở lại.

✦

Qua nhiều kỷ nguyên, các thiên thần trông nom Trái Đất mà không đòi sự sống phải biết tên mình.

Michael bước sát tới.

“Đừng.”

Giọng chàng thấp đến mức bài ca gần như nuốt mất. Thanh kiếm vẫn nằm yên. Lời ấy không buộc bất kỳ thứ gì phải dừng ngoài Lucifer.

Y nhìn bàn tay đang chảy sáng.

“Ngươi nghĩ ta chưa từng tự hỏi sao?” Michael nói. “Ta tự hỏi khi thung lũng đầu tiên im đi.”

Chàng nâng tay.

Những ngón tay trần hướng về vai Lucifer, chậm và vụng về hơn mọi động tác y từng thấy ở chàng. Bàn tay dừng giữa không trung.

Cách một gang tay.

Hơi thở Michael chao đi rồi trở về nhịp cũ.

“Đến thung lũng thứ ba,” chàng nói, “ta không còn thời gian để hỏi nữa.”

Bàn tay khép lại và hạ xuống.

Dưới quảng trường, bài ca tiếp tục mà không cần cả hai người.

Lucifer nhìn khoảng cách vừa không được vượt qua. “Ngươi vẫn muốn ta trở lại đó?”

Michael luồn những ngón tay bị thương vào chiếc găng bạc.

“Ta muốn ngươi ở lại khi câu hỏi kế tiếp đến.”

“Để làm gì?”

“Để ta nghe thấy nó trước khi nó thành lưỡi kiếm.”

Từng khớp kim loại khép lại. Vệt sáng trong lòng bàn tay biến mất sau lớp giáp.

“Ta trở lại thì điều gì thay đổi?”

Michael nhìn quảng trường.

Người giữ nốt dẫn lại hát cao hơn một chút. Một hàng cánh phía tây chậm xuống để đỡ lấy giọng ấy. Sai lệch đi qua đội hình rồi được san phẳng.

“Chưa có gì,” chàng nói.

Lucifer bật cười ngắn. “Ít nhất lần này ngươi không gọi đó là hy vọng.”

Michael quay về phía hành lang.

“Nếu hàng ngũ là nơi câu hỏi phải câm đi thì sao?” Lucifer hỏi.

Bước chân Michael dừng ở ngưỡng cửa.

Khi quay lại, gương mặt chàng đã trở về vẻ bình lặng của người chỉ huy. Chỉ có chiếc găng phải chưa khép hoàn toàn ở cổ tay.

“Hoài nghi không phải bóng tối,” Michael nói. “Nó là một cánh cửa.”

Lucifer chờ.

“Đừng để cơn giận chọn thứ bước qua.”

Michael rời ban công.

Tiếng giáp đi dọc hành lang, đều và nặng. Lucifer đứng yên cho đến khi âm thanh ấy chỉ còn là một nhịp rung dưới lòng bàn chân.

Y quay về phía Trái Đất.

Hành tinh non trẻ treo ngoài rìa những ngọn tháp, xanh sẫm dưới các dải mây tro. Từ nơi này, Lucifer có thể che khuất nó bằng đầu ngón tay.

Y không làm vậy.

Ánh sáng trên ban công đổi hướng theo bài ca bên dưới. Bóng cột đá lướt qua mặt y; phần trời quanh Trái Đất tối xuống.

Những ngôi sao hiện ra.

PROLOGUE — THE DAY HEAVEN LEARNED OF WAR

✦

The first shard of the tower fell between them.

It punched through the wing of an angel crawling away from the fissure and pinned them to the crystal floor. Their cry broke loose, then vanished beneath the clash of metal. Lucifer turned. High above, what remained of the tower had tilted from its foundations, slowly casting its shadow over both armies.

Michael saw it too. “Hold the left.”

Lucifer had no time to decide whether he still took orders from him. His wings were already open.

The wind lashed ash from the square. Across from him, Michael drove his sword into the stone. His knees buckled as the tower’s weight bore down upon the blade. Lines of light raced along his silver armor, flared where the pauldron had shattered, then went dark.

The mass of the tower halted above them—for a single beat. Lucifer raised a hand. He did not try to bear the weight Michael held; he broke the course of its fall. Thousands of plates of luminous matter ground against one another with a shriek. Half slid west, half toppled east, skimming the ranks of shields before hurtling beyond the edge of the square.

The final shard grazed Lucifer’s wing. The smell of scorched feathers mingled with the ash. When the sky opened above them again, both armies were still there.

Several looked up as though they had forgotten which direction their swords were meant to face. An angel in Michael’s ranks dropped their shield and ran to drag free the rebel warrior pinned beneath the shard. The wounded warrior jerked their hand away by instinct. For a moment they stared at one another; then both gripped the slab.

Michael did not stop them. Lucifer saw that his hand remained on the hilt of his sword.

Near the fissure, Healiangel was already kneeling beside the fallen angel. Light spilled from the pierced wing and washed over both his wrists. He bent low, almost cradling the wound to keep it from jolting as the square continued to split beneath them.

A warrior from Heaven rushed forward. Mazikeen stepped across the path, her black sword raised before the angel’s chest.

“Stand back.”

“He is one of mine.”

Mazikeen glanced down at Healiangel. “Then let him live first.”

She tipped her chin toward the healing hands.

The other angel did not retreat, but neither did they advance.

Healiangel looked at no one. “If you want him returned to you, stop making the stone shake.”

Mazikeen turned her blade toward the ground. The angel opposite her slowly lowered their weapon in answer.

A rumble passed beneath Lucifer’s feet. The fissure across the square opened wider. Light from the depths struck Michael’s face, revealing the cut that ran from his temple to his cheekbone. The wound was fresh. Lucifer recognized the path of his own blade. He remembered the force of the impact driving back through his wrist.

Michael pulled his sword from the floor.

“Enough.”

His voice was not loud. Those nearest heard it nonetheless and drew their formation tighter.

Lucifer folded his wings. The newly burned feathers rasped together, raw with pain.

“You should tell them.”

“I am speaking to you.”

Michael stepped to the edge of the fissure. A slab gave way beneath his foot and fell into the light below without a sound.

“Lower your sword.”

Lucifer looked at his hand. The blade still held the light of those it had touched. He could not remember when his grip had become so tight.

“You first.”

Michael stood motionless.

Lucifer had been waiting for that very silence. His fingers tightened again.

Behind Michael, one angel shielded a wounded comrade with their own wings. Behind Lucifer, a warrior missing half a wing forced themself upright because they saw him watching.

Michael looked across both ranks. His sword hand lowered a little. Several blades behind him followed, then stopped. Lucifer loosened his grip; when the half-winged warrior saw it, they clutched their weapon all the harder.

“Come back.”

“To be judged?”

“To live.”

Lucifer looked at the cut on his face. “You cannot promise that.”

“I can stand before you.”

“You are standing before me.”

Michael said nothing.

By the fissure, the angel beneath Healiangel’s hands gave a strangled cry. Healiangel bent closer. Mazikeen looked at Lucifer. She did not urge him. That alone made it harder for him to turn away.

Michael stepped across the fissure.

Stone shattered beneath his feet but did not fall. The gravity surrounding his armor held the fragments in place, forming a path wide enough for only one.

The formation behind him stirred.

Michael extended his empty hand.

“Come back with me.”

The sword in Lucifer’s hand lowered.

He had not meant to lower it. His wrist simply grew heavy at the sight of that hand—the hand that had once held the ground beneath his song, that had just braced an entire tower so he could turn its fall, and that now trembled almost imperceptibly in the midst of the battlefield.

A scream rose from the tier of bridges below.

Countless wings turned toward the sound. Michael’s formation closed around the fissure. On Lucifer’s side, everyone still able to stand raised their weapons and waited for him to choose first.

Michael’s hand remained open.

Lucifer looked at those fingers. Then he looked at the sword in Michael’s other hand.

“I was with you once,” he said.

“You still can be.”

“Not in the way you want.”

Michael advanced another half step. The fissure thundered beneath his feet.

“I do not want to kill you.”

Lucifer saw Michael’s jaw tighten around the words. Light seeped from the cut on his cheek and traced a narrow line downward.

“I know.”

He raised his sword.

Michael’s hand closed.

In the brief moment before Michael returned it to his sword hilt, Lucifer thought he would call him by a title. Morning Star. The Rebel. Any name distant enough to let their blades meet.

Michael called, “Samael.”

The point of Lucifer’s sword strayed from its line by the width of a knuckle. Michael saw it, but he did not step forward.

Behind them, those they had both just saved had taken up their weapons again.

Lucifer brought his sword point back into line. Michael raised his blade.

The two blades met. Beneath their feet, the fissure opened wider.

CHAPTER 1 — THE FRACTURED SYMPHONY

✦

The final note in Lucifer’s voice traveled the breadth of Heaven and returned beneath the soles of his feet.

He knew the exact beat on which it would return. Even so, when the crystal floor trembled, he waited a moment longer to hear the last echo dissolve among the towers.

Before him, the square opened between three tiers of luminous cloud. Ranks of angels stretched beyond the farthest reach of sight. Armor met armor. Wing folded behind wing. Beneath every footfall lay a bass note carved into the stone; every unfurling wing rang like metal leaving a sheath, joining the next until sound covered the sky.

Lucifer raised his hand.

The golden river at the foot of the tower rose from its banks and curved above the square. The first note of his song touched it. Light divided into countless threads, ran through the ranks, then returned bearing the smallest imperfections caught within them.

Three guardian angels at the base of the western tower had held their breath too long. A Seraph on the upper tier had opened its wings before the cue. Farther away, a bass voice dropped nearly half a tone as the sound crossed armor newly forged.

Lucifer turned his wrist.

The golden river changed course, struck the face of the tower, and rebounded. Three breaths released. The wings above paused for precisely one beat. The bass found its pitch again without anyone in the ranks having to turn toward the one who had sung astray.

At the far end of the square, Michael lowered the point of his sword to the floor.

He did not conduct the melody. He held what lay beneath it. Whenever the harmony rose too high, weight from the silver sword pressed a fine groove into the crystal; whenever light spilled from the formation, one movement of his shoulder drew it back, clean as the closing edge of armor.

Lucifer lifted the music.

Michael gave it somewhere to land.

They had done this through so many ages that neither needed to look at the other. Yet at the final change of key, Michael still raised his eyes. Lucifer caught his gaze amid a million wings. Michael inclined his head by the slightest degree. Lucifer lowered his final finger.

The multitude of voices closed as one.

The last note crossed the valleys, rippled the surfaces of the golden rivers, and reached the farthest rim of Heaven. When it returned, it was as whole as when it had left the square.

Lucifer let his hand fall.

A spear struck the ground.

The sound was thin, dry, and out of place. Several ranks near the rear of the square turned before discipline pulled them back into position.

The angel newly returned from the frontier knelt on one knee. The spear lay beside them, flickering against the stone. Their companion bent and took hold of their elbow.

“Stand.”

The word was too quiet to travel far. The sentinel braced a hand against the floor. Their knee slipped. Light still shone within their chest, but its rhythm did not match the breaths breaking through parted lips.

Michael stepped out of position.

His weight sent a dark line spreading beneath the crystal. He looked at the sentinel, then at Lucifer.

The next movement of the hymn already lay open before him. He had only to lower his hand and the entire square would enter the first note. If he withheld it, the countless ranks would be forced to stand within a pause no rite had ever known.

Lucifer watched the hands trembling around the spear shaft.

The angel rose without aid before he could decide. Their companion released their elbow and stepped back into place. The ranks closed so quickly that the abandoned space vanished among the shining armor.

Michael had not yet returned to the line.

Lucifer lowered his hand.

The hymn continued.

When the sentinel’s turn came, their voice entered half a beat late.

The angel beside them did not look over. Michael remained still for another moment before returning to his place. Only Lucifer kept the deviation in his ear.

Those who guarded the rim called the places from which they had returned the silences. No map recorded them. Light still existed there, but without warmth; the sound of wings vanished directly behind you; the bond joining every angel to the hymn receded until even the weapon in your grasp became alien.

Once outside, everything returned at once. Some fell. Others went back to formation and never spoke of what had happened.

Lucifer had never entered one of the silences. He heard only the marks they left behind: a breath that would not return to measure, wings folded too tightly, a note arriving late from one who had never sung false.

Across the square, the hymn remained radiant and full.

The missing half beat did not vanish within it.

✦

What Lucifer remembered most clearly of the First Giants was the warmth left in his palm.

When Earth was still dark green with ferns and primeval forests, a convulsion of the ground had closed two mountain walls around a young giant. Its foreleg was trapped beneath a slab of volcanic rock. Each time it struggled, more stone tumbled down the slope, and its cries crossed the marshes in rings that trembled over the water.

Lucifer descended through the rain.

Wind from his golden wings forced the ancient trees to bow. Dead leaves swept from the earth. Stones around his feet tore free of the mud and hung suspended.

The creature saw all of it.

It flung up its head, its long neck smashing through a tree. The trapped leg wrenched hard. The stone bit deeper into its scaled hide, and black blood poured into the mud.

Lucifer stopped.

The slab was nothing to him. With the closing of one finger, he could have ground it into sand. But in the creature’s wide black eyes, he was only another source of light descending amid a world that shook.

He drew in his wings.

Rain fell upon his shoulders again and darkened his hair. The stones suspended around him dropped into the mud one by one.

Lucifer stepped forward.

The creature roared. Heat from its mouth blasted the water from the leaves.

He stopped.

It jerked its leg again. Its entire body curled around the wound.

“I know.”

The words could carry no meaning to it, but his voice had lowered, emptied of the force with which he led a million voices.

Lucifer placed one knee in the mud and opened his hand.

Beyond the mountain wall, the call of the herd echoed. The young giant answered with a brief sound, then fell silent. It studied the hand before it for a long while. Rain followed the grooves of its brow and dripped between Lucifer’s fingers.

The immense neck slowly lowered.

Its cold, rain-soaked brow touched his luminous palm. The heart beneath the bone beat so powerfully that Lucifer felt the pulse climb into his wrist.

He waited.

Only when the rhythm slowed did Lucifer extend his other hand toward the slab. The volcanic rock rose without a sound. The creature dragged its leg free, staggered backward, and collapsed to its knees. Lucifer kept the stone suspended until it could stand by itself.

It did not flee at once.

Its long muzzle reached forward and touched his shoulder. Mud, blood, and hot breath covered the radiant robe that no rite of Heaven had ever allowed to bear a stain.

A very soft sound escaped Lucifer. Later, he would not remember whether it had been laughter.

Beyond the mountain, the herd called again. The creature turned. It managed three steps, its foreleg still carving a long furrow through the earth, then stopped and looked back at him.

Lucifer inclined his head.

The creature disappeared into the rain.

He carried the scent of wet earth back to Heaven. It had vanished from his skin before he reached the first step, but the warmth remained.

✦

Through age after age, the angels watched over Earth without asking that its living creatures know their names.

They turned ash away from water, braced collapsing mountainsides, and lifted the winds so winged herds could cross regions of fire. Across the plains, bodies longer than Heaven’s towers shook the ground with every step. In the deep seas, giants glided like mountains that had learned to hunt.

Not every angel remembered every living thing. A duty passed through them, was completed, and returned to order as a note returned to its chord.

Lucifer remembered.

He remembered the flooded tracks beside the rivers, the calls of herds in the mist, and the heartbeat that had once struck his palm beneath the rain.

On the day that age ended, no voice crossed the sky.

The constellations at Heaven’s rim shifted from their stations. Towers of luminous matter descended into a bass register never used in any rite. The golden rivers went still, so flat they no longer reflected the wings passing overhead.

Lucifer stood at the center of the square as the decree passed through Heaven.

The knees of the countless ranks touched the floor as one. He knelt with them. No words sounded, yet he felt the command in the bones of his wings and in the pulse of light behind his chest:

The old age was ended.

Earth must be prepared for what came after.

In a rank near Lucifer, an angel newly returned from the deep sea bowed their head. Salt water still clung to the armor around their throat. Beside them, wings scored by a long, unhealed gash folded tight.

The chorus rose.

When his note came, Lucifer looked into his palm. No mud, blood, or trace of touch remained there.

His voice entered one beat late.

Michael looked up from the far side of the square.

Another voice in the ranks faltered with Lucifer’s, then hurried back into place. The others passed over the deviation. The music continued to rise, coiling around the towers and descending upon the world below like a seal set in place.

On Earth, the sky opened into fire.

A mass of stone from beyond the heavens tore through the clouds. Its light cast the shadows of the giant herds across the ground before the sound of impact arrived. The seas stood upright. Ancient forests were ripped from their roots. Burning stone fell through the atmosphere, reddened, and shattered into countless smaller fragments—enough to set ablaze every land the waves had not swallowed.

The angels spread their wings above a world changing shape.

They held collapsing reaches of sky long enough to turn the rivers of fire away from those veins of life permitted to endure, then carried seeds smaller than a fingernail through winds that could strip stone from mountains.

They could move oceans, but they could not call an age back into being.

In the north, Michael stood beneath a rupture spreading across the sky. He drove his sword into empty space. The air around the blade hardened, layer upon layer, like metal quenched in cold.

Beneath his wings, three valleys still rang with life.

Michael held the rupture. Half of it had closed. Lines of light raced along his arm, threaded beneath the plates of his armor, and burst out at the elbow. The sword shook in his hand; every time it strayed by the width of a finger joint, the sky below sank farther.

He forced it back.

In the eastern valley, a herd running along the riverbank had turned to vapor. In the west, winged creatures swirled into a black cloud, beating again and again against an invisible current of heat. In the middle valley, a young creature fell within the river of fire. Its mother ran past it, stopped, and turned back.

Michael saw.

He changed his footing. The atmosphere hollowed beneath him. The rupture closed a little farther, but a line of light recoiled from the hilt, cut across his palm, and raced into his wing.

He could hold longer.

Michael knew exactly how much longer his body could endure.

Then the weight of the world changed direction and bore down upon each of Michael’s fingers.

The sword remained in place.

The mother in the middle valley had returned to her young. She nudged the smaller body with her head, once, then once again.

Michael’s fingers opened.

The sword left the rupture. The sky folded down.

The eastern valley fell silent first. The western valley followed. In the middle, the mother’s call lasted one beat longer before the fire swallowed it.

Michael remained suspended in the air. The hand that had released the sword could not close again at once.

✦

Lucifer found the giant he had known upon a plain covered in ash.

It had grown through many ages. The neck that had once risen above the treetops could now see beyond the crowns of an entire primeval forest. The ridges of bone along its back stood as high as fortress walls. One foreleg still left a faint drag mark in the earth—the old wound had healed, but it had never wholly disappeared.

The creature stood among blackened trunks and turned toward Lucifer as he descended.

It recognized him.

It lowered its immense head, though its forelegs did not bend. The gesture had happened once beneath the rain; the body remembered it longer than any name.

He approached.

Light gathered in his palm.

It died before it could touch the creature.

Lucifer stopped. He spread his wings and called down more power from the radiant reaches above. Ash recoiled from his feet, leaving a ring of bare earth. Burned trees leaned away. This time the light traveled along his arm, gathered at his wrist, then folded inward like a river striking a wall without form.

Pain lanced to his elbow.

He tried again.

The giant stepped toward him.

Its knees sank deep into the hot earth. A sheet of charred hide peeled from its flank with the movement. Breath thick with blood and ash left its mouth, so heavy that the ground before Lucifer’s feet trembled.

“Stop.”

The creature kept coming.

Lucifer thrust both hands toward it. The power that had once turned falling stones of heaven poured from the bones of his wings into his palms, bright enough to cast the burned trees as black lines across the ash.

The light stopped a handspan from the creature.

Lucifer clenched his teeth and forced more into it. The light within his wing bones closed, wrenching all his power back like flesh sealing around a wound.

A fissure of light split from his wrist. Luminous blood fell into the ash and burned in tiny embers.

The giant had come close enough. Its brow lowered, searching for the hand that had once rested there.

“Don’t.”

This time Lucifer did not know whether he spoke to the creature or to the part of himself that had just refused to go farther.

Half a handspan remained.

A shock passed across the plain. On the horizon, a mountain range folded down. Hot wind snapped Lucifer’s wings open, but he did not retreat.

The creature exhaled.

Its final breath held only enough force to stir the ash across his open fingertips.

The heavy head fell before his feet. Its brow struck the earth beyond the barrier of light it could not cross.

Lucifer kept his hand there.

Power withdrew from his wrist. The stones hanging in the air fell one by one. Only when the final sound sank into the ash did he hear how silent the plain had become.

The creature no longer knew he stood before it.

He crossed the distance between them.

Nothing barred him now.

Lucifer knelt and placed his hand upon its brow. The hide still held warmth, but the heart whose pulse had once climbed into his wrist beneath the rain was still.

He remained there until ash coated his golden wings.

An angel descended behind him. A burn ran the length of their breastplate, and they held a blackened feather in one hand. Footsteps approached, then stopped.

Lucifer did not turn.

After a time, the angel left. The feather remained in their hand.

✦

When the armies returned, Heaven had already begun the hymn of the new age.

The golden rivers moved once more. Armor was washed in the current of light beneath the Throne Hall; ash flowed from the channels in the metal and vanished before reaching the bank. Formations assembled across the square, filling the places of those who had not returned.

Lucifer stood outside the first rank.

He watched the angels emerge from the river. One submerged both wrists and kept them there longer than needed. Another washed only their armor, leaving a thin gray trace beneath the nails. The angel who had descended behind Lucifer still clenched the burned feather in one fist.

Another saw it. Their eyes met, then both looked away.

No one came to stand beside Lucifer, and no one had yet found a common name for what they carried.

At the head of the square, the conducting arm rose. The ranks of wings opened.

The hymn began.

The voice holding Lucifer’s leading note was bright and exact. The ranks followed without wavering. When the angel with the feather entered, their voice left their lips thinner than before.

Lucifer heard it. In other ranks, several breaths also failed to enter at once. The hymn did not break; only the echo that returned no longer matched the sound that had departed.

He turned from the square before the movement ended.

✦

Lucifer heard the hymn change conductors before Michael’s footsteps reached the corridor.

His note remained. Another Seraph held it, slightly low at the end of each measure but close enough that the multitude below could not recognize the absence that had just been filled.

Lucifer placed a hand on the balustrade.

The marble was cold, smooth, and clean. Ash on his fingertips left no mark. He pressed harder. A small fracture traveled through the heart of the stone and stopped beneath the skin of his palm.

“You left the leading note empty.”

Michael stood at the entrance to the balcony. He still wore the armor he had taken to Earth, but his right hand was bare. The silver gauntlet rested in his left, dented across the knuckles.

Lucifer looked down into the square. “They have replaced me.”

“They are holding your place.”

“A place that needs another to hold it is no longer what it was.”

Michael did not answer. His gaze settled upon a grain of ash caught among the golden feathers. The thumb rubbing the gauntlet’s joint went still.

“Come back,” he said.

“I have not left Heaven.”

“You know what I mean.”

Below, a drumbeat of light crossed the square. Every formation changed step. The movement was so perfect that the tower floor trembled exactly once, then fell still.

“The hymn is not over,” Michael said.

Lucifer turned. “The three northern valleys are.”

Light from the square traveled along the edges of Michael’s silver armor, but it could not reach his bare hand.

“I heard them fall silent.”

“You were not there.”

“I was close enough.”

“No.”

The answer escaped more quickly than Michael’s usual measure.

He went to the balustrade and set his bare hand where Lucifer’s had just released it. His knuckles slowly whitened.

“I held the rupture,” he said. “Half of it had closed.”

Lucifer waited.

Michael looked down at his hand.

“Then I let go.”

Lucifer had carried the question all the way back, honing it into an edge to set between them. Now that Michael had offered him the hilt, he could not lift it.

“The eastern valley fell silent first,” Michael said. “In the middle valley, one of the young fell in the fire. Its mother ran past it.”

His voice stopped.

A hairline fracture crept from beneath the thumb pressing into the marble.

“She turned back,” Michael said.

“And still you let go.”

“Yes.”

“Then you came back here.”

“Yes.”

The answer was too brief to give Lucifer a clean place to strike.

“Why?”

Michael looked at the ranks still singing.

“The formation remained standing.”

“Those living creatures had stood once.”

“I know.”

“Do not speak as though knowing were enough.”

“It is not.”

This time Michael turned fully toward him. Beneath his eyes lay a darkness Heaven’s light could not erase. His armor had been washed clean, but the bare hand remained red across the joints, as though he had scrubbed the metal too long beneath the golden river.

“I chose the formation,” Michael said.

Lucifer fell silent.

Michael forced himself to finish.

“And I let the three valleys die.”

No drumbeat sounded at that moment. The hymn below continued, radiant and exact, as though the confession could not bend even one measure of the rite.

A dry breath escaped Lucifer.

“At last you have named it.”

“Naming it will not restore them.”

“No. But at least the one who saw them has not vanished entirely beneath the armor.”

Michael turned toward the exit.

Lucifer stepped into his path.

The balcony rumbled. The patterns carved into the columns lost their color for one beat, then brightened again. Michael did not reach for his sword.

“Move.”

“I came back as well,” Lucifer said. “I stood in the ranks. I sang while ash was still in my mouth.”

“I know.”

“You saw me sing. You do not know what I left behind before I could make a sound.”

Michael tightened his grip on the gauntlet. An edge of metal pressed into his skin.

“Then what do you want from me?”

From the square below, the leading note rose slightly too high. The one holding Lucifer’s place tried to correct the deviation, making the whole chorus brighter and thinner.

Lucifer heard every place where it strained.

“I want to know whether the one who saw still lives inside the commander who returned.”

Michael held his gaze.

“If that commander breaks, who keeps those still standing?”

“You always ask who will hold them. You never ask how long they must live beneath the hand that holds them.”

Michael closed his eyes.

The silver gauntlet twisted in his grip. A drop of light welled where its edge cut into his palm.

Lucifer could stop.

He did not.

“You call it order because the sword is in your hand.”

Michael opened his eyes.

“I carry it so those without swords may remain standing.”

“The three valleys had no swords.”

Michael stepped close.

“Don’t.”

His voice was so low the hymn nearly swallowed it. The sword remained still. The word compelled nothing to stop except Lucifer.

He looked at Michael’s hand, bleeding light.

“Do you think I never questioned it?” Michael said. “I questioned it when the first valley fell silent.”

He raised his hand.

The bare fingers reached toward Lucifer’s shoulder, slower and more uncertain than any movement Lucifer had ever seen from him. The hand stopped in the air.

One handspan away.

Michael’s breath faltered, then returned to measure.

“By the third valley,” he said, “there was no time left to ask.”

The hand closed and fell.

Below, the hymn continued without either of them.

Lucifer looked at the distance that had not been crossed. “And you still want me to return?”

Michael slid his wounded fingers into the silver gauntlet.

“I want you to remain when the next question comes.”

“For what?”

“So I can hear it before it becomes a blade.”

Each metal joint closed into place. The line of light in his palm vanished beneath the armor.

“If I return, what changes?”

Michael looked toward the square.

The one holding the leading note sang too high again. A western rank slowed to support the voice. The deviation traveled through the formation and was smoothed away.

“Nothing yet,” he said.

Lucifer gave a short laugh. “At least this time you did not call it hope.”

Michael turned toward the corridor.

“What if the ranks are where questions must fall silent?” Lucifer asked.

Michael’s footstep stopped at the threshold.

When he turned, his face had regained the stillness of a commander. Only the right gauntlet remained imperfectly closed at the wrist.

“Doubt is not darkness,” Michael said. “It is a door.”

Lucifer waited.

“Do not let anger choose what passes through.”

Michael left the balcony.

The sound of armor moved down the corridor, even and heavy. Lucifer remained still until it became only a pulse beneath the soles of his feet.

He turned toward Earth.

The young planet hung beyond the outermost towers, dark green beneath bands of ashen cloud. From there, Lucifer could have covered it with the tip of one finger.

He did not.

Light shifted across the balcony with the hymn below. The shadow of a column passed over his face; the sky around Earth darkened.

The stars appeared.
